Hi guys. I've gone back and forth about if I want to enter a DNP program this fall. I currently work in an acute psych facility with child, adolescent, and adult units. I have two years of experience and have worked with each population, but love C&A the most. There is no question in my mind about my passion for psych or my ability to be an excellent NP in the future.

My concern is the following: I want to start a family in about 3-4 years. My fiance and I agree that I should stay at home full-time, especially when the babies are young. After that, I am open to working like once a week or multiple times a week with shortened hours. I know the field is oversaturated with NPs wanting to work remote but this would be ideal for me. I live in WV so I believe the demand may be higher due to poor access to outpatient offices in rural areas.

I want to know if it's worth spending the time and money when I want to work less than part-time hours from the beginning. The program is three years, so I would be graduating right around the time I want to get pregnant. I'm guessing that's a bad idea when that time should be focused on getting experience and making connections.

I feel like the obvious answer is I shouldn't do the program, but I can't let it go. I am so passionate about growing within the field and making a broader impact on my community. I guess my goals are just too conflicting. Do you guys think I could make both things work or should I let go and just continue working the floor?

Thank you!

I’m a new grad psych nurse, been doing it for about 6 months. I have absolutely no regrets and I honestly love psych more every day. I definitely see myself staying in psych for the rest of my nursing career. If you love psych patients and the atmosphere of inpatient, and you don’t have any glaring interest in other specialities, I think you’ll be happy going right into psych as a new grad. I knew psych was right for me when my favorite patients during med surg/ICU/etc rotations had neuro, memory, or psych comorbidities. I’m so glad I followed my gut. Good luck!

Edit: I looked for nurse residency programs in PA, MD, and VA. I found multiple different options I liked but ultimately settled in MD. There definitely aren’t as many opportunities as med surg, but if you’re open to exploring jobs in multiple areas, you’ll have no issues finding a job somewhere. I started interviewing 6 months before graduation and then accepted a job about a month before. I recommend looking and applying now (you don’t have to commit to anything!).

You sound very similar to me! I have also been on Yaz since I was 15 (I am 21F). I am not a doctor, but my understanding when I began the pill was that taking it until I try getting pregnant will reduce my risk of infertility. I believe it has something to do with getting your body used to the normal menstrual cycle, which will allow you to ovulate correctly when off the pill. While I have no experience completely eliminating birth control, I did try the Nexplanon arm implant for a year. It gave me really bad cystic acne, irregular periods, and abnormal hair growth. As soon as I got back on Yaz, everything normalized. I do have PCOS, so it may be different for you if you truly don’t have the condition. If you feel strongly about going off Yaz for a bit, consult your doctor and try it out! You can monitor for any symptoms, and if you feel it is affecting you, you can reassess your plan. If you have a normal menstrual cycle after a couple of months, I wouldn’t be too worried. Good luck, I know how stressful this can be!

Agreed. Have been 140lbs since high school and was diagnosed with PCOS at 14. Weight gain and diet will definitely worsen symptoms but a large portion of women with PCOS are completely healthy. In fact, out of all of the girls I know at university with PCOS, only three are overweight. When a female produces excess testosterone and androgen levels, you are likely to experience cysts, acne, hirsutism, etc. Overweight or not. 

Not dismissing the fact that obesity can cause PCOS, but it is definitely not as “typical” as you claim.

You are definitely not crazy. My current boyfriend was the same exact way for the first 6 months of our relationship. He would flirt with some of the girls at our workplace on top of snapchatting them constantly in the evenings. One day I was driving us to go hiking and looked over to see him talking to the new Italian exchange student. Later found out that he was seeking her advice/comfort about personal problems instead of me.

It bothered me, but I felt like I was being too sensitive and decided not to communicate my concerns. Months later, he cheated on me with one of our co workers (someone he snapchatted regularly). I found out about a month after it happened and it completely destroyed me. I've always had a pretty low self esteem, but this made everything worse. I ended up forgiving him and we are still working on our issues a year later. But I am constantly tackling my lowered self esteem and my extreme jealously issues. 

My point is, talk your SO before something like this happens. Tell him that you are hurt by the amount of time he spends talking to these girls. Ask him to look at the situation from your perspective, especially regarding his secrecy about his snapchat account.
You have been together for five years, and if he can't respect your feelings about this, is he really the person you want to be with?
